A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LAMP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched despite relocated references and renumbered supplementary sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original LAMP trajectory evaluations, ablations, generated-video examples and a 16-participant user study, including Tables 1–6 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds demonstrations with three video generators and a quantitative DSL failure analysis.

M1.justification: The object-then-camera planning factorization, four DSL primitives, deterministic trajectory conversion and control-video pipeline remain unchanged. Tables 7–10 retain the same DSL specification; the additional generator demonstrations do not document a changed planning algorithm.

E1.justification: The procedural corpus, DataDoP, ET and CameraBench coverage remains. Supplementary Section 3 and Figure 11 add an explicit video-to-video camera-control demonstration with ReCamMaster alongside text-to-video and image-to-video portability examples.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the trajectory evaluations, ablations and user study are unchanged. CameraCtrl, EPiC and ReCamMaster in the new demonstrations serve as downstream generators using LAMP outputs, rather than competing motion planners.

E3.justification: v3 adds testing with three pretrained generators and a DSL-validity evaluation described as four datasets with 10,000 captions each, although those datasets are not named. Existing benchmark and user-study protocols remain; the revised DataDoP F1 procedure was already documented in v1 Supplementary Section B.1.

E4.justification: New supplementary analyses examine whether DSL outputs work across different generators and how often generated tags contain motion-type confusions or invalid syntax. The DSL-versus-trajectory ablation and dataset-training analyses in Tables 4–6 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added failure counts are point results and sample-size information, without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds Figure 11's generator examples and a reported 0.11% DSL failure rate, comprising 3 motion-type confusions and 8 invalid tags per 10,000 samples. Section 4.3 changes the GPT-DSL 'both preferred' percentage from 35% to 25%, consistent with unchanged Figure 6. Table 1's revised F1 values were already present in v1 Table 5, so they are not new performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the symbolic sequence definitions and the DSL's formal specification are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs, and the revised F1 rationale already appears in v1's appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: joint object-camera planning through a cinematographic DSL, procedural training data and editable motion control. The new supplementary evidence supports this existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 reinterpret DataDoP performance as superior rather than comparable, while the new failure analysis argues for DSL stability. Section 3.3 removes the single-primary-object caveat, although the appendix retains manual multi-object alignment and video-generator adherence limitations.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies Qwen2.5-VL-7B and VACE-1.3B for the existing runtime descriptions and provides a project-page link stating code and video availability. Conversely, Section 3.4 drops the 35%/30%/35% primitive-mixture proportions and unique-tag counts used for paraphrasing. These are documentation changes, without evidence of changed underlying settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds SAGE as a cited cinematographic inbetweening approach in Section 2 and the bibliography. The remaining cited works and the central positioning of LAMP relative to trajectory predictors and video generators are retained.

P1.justification: v3 selectively condenses the corpus description, evaluation prose and limitations, expands the first author's name and adds acknowledgements. References move after the supplement, whose sections are renumbered; most wording and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 11 and restructures Table 1 with separate revised and original F1 columns. Existing figures and tables are retained, with adjustments to placement, sizing, captions and page layout.

improvement.justification: The generator demonstrations and quantified DSL failures add modest empirical support, while the corrected user-study percentage resolves an inconsistency with Figure 6. Model-size disclosures and project-page access information improve documentation. These gains are tempered by removed sampling details, unnamed datasets in the failure analysis and broader DataDoP superiority wording despite mixed Coverage/FID results. The central benchmark evidence, including revised F1 scores, was already present in v1.
